topic: DNACPR and ceilings of care documentation
usual_baseline: Forms exist but are incomplete. None fully completed and 48% not endorsed by a consultant [1917]. 63.8% signed only by an NCHD [1892]. DNAR status in medical notes 35%, reasoning 32% [1850]. Discussion with patient often missing: 41% undocumented [1917]. Ceilings of care under 15% [1850].
fix_that_works: Redesigning the form. Moving the treatment escalation plan to the front page of a new DNACPR form raised TEPs from 56% to 99% of patients not for CPR, with doctor's name and grade on every form [1816].
fix_that_fails: Two education sessions left DNAR status (35%) and reasoning (32%) unchanged. Relatives' discussion stayed at 48% and ceilings of care stayed under 15% [1850][1872]. After the redesign, 83.3% of patients still had no documented resuscitation status [1816].
consultant_advice: Most of these audits are single-cycle, and teaching alone did not move the numbers. More useful: audit how many patients who need a decision have one at all, or add resuscitation and escalation status to the ward round proforma [3494]. Note [1850] and [1872] report the same audit.
